candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: MediaReview
candidates.comment: A specialized review dedicated to evaluating online media content, often in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. Also called media fact-check, content authenticity review, misinformation analysis. Examples: a fact-check of a viral video, an analysis of a manipulated image, a review of a misleading news article. Distinct from Review, which is a general evaluation of any item or service.

candidates.label: CorrectionComment
candidates.comment: A CorrectionComment is a specific type of comment that provides corrections or amendments to a CreativeWork. Also called erratum, amendment, revision note. Examples: A correction notice on an online article, an errata sheet for a book, a revised caption for an image.

types.oie_definition: The sequence of professional experiences and jobs held by an individual throughout their working life.
types.embedding_query_text: Career: The sequence of professional experiences and jobs held by an individual throughout their working life. Also called profession, occupation, work history.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Occupation class explicitly lists 'career' as an 'also called' term and its definition aligns well.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: OccupationalExperienceRequirements
candidates.comment: OccupationalExperienceRequirements is an intangible entity indicating employment-related experience requirements. Also called job experience, work experience criteria, professional background. Examples: '5 years of experience in software development', 'entry-level position', 'management experience required'. Distinct from EducationalOccupationalCredential, which specifies formal qualifications.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.oie_definition: A business entity that produces and distributes content related to sports across various media platforms.
types.embedding_query_text: Sports Media Company: A business entity that produces and distributes content related to sports across various media platforms. Also called sports broadcaster, athletic media outlet, sports network.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: A sports media company is an organization that produces and disseminates news/content, fitting the NewsMediaOrganization class.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.oie_definition: A program broadcast on television.
types.embedding_query_text: TV Show: A program broadcast on television. Also called television program, broadcast series, telecast.

chosen_type.label: TVSeries
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org TVSeries class explicitly lists 'television show' as an 'also called' term and its definition matches.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: TelevisionStation
candidates.comment: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.

candidates.label: TVEpisode
candidates.comment: A single installment of a television series, typically part of a season. Also called television episode, show episode, broadcast installment. Examples: 'The Pilot' episode of a new series, 'Episode 5 of Season 2' of a drama.

candidates.label: TelevisionChannel
candidates.comment: A unique instance of a television broadcast service on a cable or satellite lineup. Also called TV channel, broadcast channel, cable channel, satellite channel. Examples: 'HBO', 'CNN', 'BBC One', 'ESPN'.

types.oie_definition: An activity involving physical exertion and skill in which an individual or team competes against another or others for entertainment.
types.embedding_query_text: Sport: An activity involving physical exertion and skill in which an individual or team competes against another or others for entertainment. Also called athletic activity, game, physical contest.

chosen_type.label: Sport
chosen_type.definition: An activity involving physical exertion and skill in which an individual or team competes against another or others for entertainment.
chosen_type.justification: Existing candidates are for events, actions, or specific types of games (e.g., board games), not the abstract concept of a sport itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: PlayAction
candidates.comment: PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising. Examples: playing a sport, performing music on stage, training for a marathon, engaging in a hobby. Distinct from ListenAction, which is consuming music; Distinct from WatchAction, which is consuming visual content.

candidates.label: ExerciseAction
candidates.comment: ExerciseAction is a PlayAction representing the act of participating in exertive activity to improve health and fitness. Also called working out, physical activity, training. Examples: Going for a run, lifting weights, practicing yoga, swimming laps.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

types.oie_definition: One of the world's main continuous expanses of land.
types.embedding_query_text: Continent: One of the world's main continuous expanses of land. Also called landmass, major land area, global region.

chosen_type.label: Continent
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org Continent class directly matches the OIE type and its definition, and the mention is a valid instance.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Mountain
candidates.comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation

candidates.label: TieAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.

types.oie_definition: An unroofed, usually oval-shaped structure with tiers of seats for spectators, used for sporting events and concerts.
types.embedding_query_text: Stadium: An unroofed, usually oval-shaped structure with tiers of seats for spectators, used for sporting events and concerts. Also called arena, sports venue, coliseum.

chosen_type.label: StadiumOrArena
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org StadiumOrArena class directly matches the OIE type and its definition, and the mention is a valid instance.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.
